sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the code page
sections.what: Brings in routing, form, validation, the input, button, notifications and the API helper.
sections.why: Standard setup. Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: VerifyOtpPage (part 1)
sections.title: Development code fetch and verify submit
sections.what: Keeps the page state, reads the email from the address, and in development asks the backend for the latest code. Submitting checks the code with the backend and goes to sign-in on success.
sections.why: The comment says the fetch exists for developer helpers.
sections.watch_out: The page hides the helper outside development but the request itself is only blocked by the backend. Confirm that.

sections.name: VerifyOtpPage (part 2)
sections.title: Resend code and developer helper box
sections.what: Requests a new code and shows a notice box in development with the code and a button that fills it in.
sections.why: The helper text explains that development mode runs without email sending.
sections.watch_out: The helper box appears only when the page thinks it is in development, so a wrong check would show the code to anyone.

sections.name: VerifyOtpPage (part 3)
sections.title: Code entry form and navigation links
sections.what: Shows the six-digit code field, the verify button, the resend link and a link to change the email address.
sections.why: Standard verification form. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The change email link goes back in history, so it may not work if the page was opened directly.

summary: The page where a new user types the six-digit code emailed to them. In local development it can show the code and fill it in.
purpose: Confirms the person owns the email address before activating the account.
why: Likely reason: the code proves email ownership. The developer helper lets testers skip real email. Reason for the helper is stated in its comment.
how: Reads the email from the address. In development, asks the backend for the latest code and shows it. Submitting verifies the code and goes to sign-in on success. Resend asks for a new code. Change email goes back a page.
inputs: The email in the address, and the six-digit code typed in.
outputs: Calls the verify and resend endpoints, shows messages, and redirects on success.
risks: In development the page fetches the live code from the backend. The page only hides this helper outside development; the backend must refuse the request in production. This is not visible here.
debug: If the helper does not appear, check the email in the address and the dev endpoint. If verification fails, check the message the backend returns.
